notes.title: Developer Diary #3
notes.content:
[i]This developer diary will be mirrored on the [url=http://www.reddit.com/r/MovieMaven]Movie Maven Tycoon subreddit[/url].
[/i]
 
Despite the chaos of the past few months our team is back hard at work and making great progress, especially in these past two weeks. Our first beta build will focus on balancing some of the core mechanics of Movie Maven. We are pushing hard to include an assignments tab framework in this build, but Franchising, Save Game, some newer art/transitions, and the tutorial will not be in this initial offering. That's right, like a hamster being cared for by preschooler, there is no end to the deprivation we will be forcing onto our bright-eyed beta testers. And on that happy note we come to our next Dev Diary.
 


[b]Box Office[/b]

The simulated Box Office environment we have created for Movie Maven is something I am especially proud of. It is one of the core components of the game and is the primary gauge on how your movies are performing.

We put a lot of features to make this Box Office feel alive and realistic. We developed a sophisticated syntax algorithm to name films from rival studios. Each NPC movie has attributes (hidden) that affect how it performs on charts, these attributes also determine which movies get nominated at the end of the year for awards. NPC movies play by the some rules as player movies. Day by day ticket receipts change depending on the day of the week with Fridays and Saturdays being the best, and even Sundays being a significant boost over the normal weekdays. I am telling you this Box Office simulation [i]slices [/i]AND [i]dices[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/51eb53888cbc20d4f053cec2dfc9fd3c7521f5d1.jpg[/img]

In addition it is always running in the background, even if you aren't looking at it. While it is extremely unlikely (but possible) that you first few films will even register onto the top 10 charts, I can attest there is nothing comparable to the pride of seeing your first movie claw its way up (perhaps the joy of holding your firstborn?). 

And [i]clawing its way up[/i] is something that will actually happen to your movies. Later in the game when you can afford marketing budgets, you will become use to opening in the top ten, but even small films with no marketing will generate hype if they are really good, and that hype will grow for several weeks perhaps pushing your movie into relevance. You can even track how your average theater attendance is doing in real time:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/ed6599ef67a518d978e86595107f0eaeb7a799fe.jpg[/img]




[b]Marketing[/b]

There are seven regions in Movie Maven, and marketing can be focused or spread out through any combination of them. As you gain research and insights you may find that certain films do better in certain regions and focus your marketing efforts in those areas. Marketing is expensive though and can easily outstrip the actual cost of the movie if you are not careful.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/ccdeef3a3477ad767fc46f78d03dcf454436b082.jpg[/img]

Micro-managing the budget so that you are not overspending as you build up hype levels in each region can help keep costs under control. But if you just leave a campaign at 100% and walk away it will cost your studio a lot of money. Until your studio gains insights and research you may not even want to bother with the expense, as it is only one portion of making a successful blockbuster.

When designing this mechanic we didn't want it to be just one more slider or button to press, we wanted it to have meaning. A marketing campaign will help a horrible movie have a strong weekend, and may help you break even on what would otherwise have been a disaster. If you find that the RNG is going south on a big investment, and a lot of bad scenes are piling up, it may be time to break out a $50 million nationwide marketing campaign.

Marketing can only do so much though, and a bad movie will still see a big drop off in ticket sales if the quality doesn't match the hype. Even with a well managed marketing campaign, very little money will be made if no theaters are carrying your movie. That bring us to Theater Networks.




[b]Theater Networks[/b]

As discussed above marketing is broken into seven regions, and so are theater networks. Each region starts with access available to approximately 50 independent theaters, for a total of about 350 nationwide. As your studio builds clout with successful movies and building up successful actors, you will be able to leverage that clout to sign contracts with larger theater chains.

More Theaters = More Screens

More Screens = More Eyeballs

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/90a59665a45abc6cff3963ba40ba018d9a6975f9.jpg[/img]

The amount of screens allotted to each chain is randomized through every playthrough. As you expand your networks you will find you are reaching larger percentages of the country, But clout is a precious resource needed for other priorities. A smart studio manager will orchestrate their expansion with purpose.

notes.title: Developer Diary #2
notes.content:
[i]This developer diary will be mirrored on the [url=http://www.reddit.com/r/MovieMaven]Movie Maven Tycoon subreddit[/url].
[/i]
 
While there are a lot of features and moving parts of Movie Mave: A Tycoon Game, the most fundamental are your employees. In this dev diary we are going to talk about Actors, Directors, and Staff members, all of which are represented differently in throughout the game. 
 


[b]Actors [/b]

A huge part of the game is centered around auditioning, cultivating, and specializing a roster of actors.  Actors come in two flavors, those you hire who owe their loyalty to your studio, and those you hire for one off productions. After a successful audition you will be given a choice of actors you would like to hire. The more money you spend on the audition process the better chance of attracting actors with higher initial experience. These actors represent those your studio have signed on to build into super stars. If you do not have an appropriate actor for a film, you can always use your clout to audition an actor for just one movie (more on clout in a later dev diary). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/a5a3d135a48da4f831e7ab567f414a448ae7b9f0.png[/img]

As you cast your actors in different films they will gain more experience, specifically talent and gravitas. As they gain more talent, a greater array of skills and perks will become available to them, allowing you to cultivate actors for media blitzes, box office boosts, clout maximization, or any other strategy your studio chooses to pursue. By the final tier you will be able to specialize actors to a single genre letting them become Sex Symbols, Action Stars, and more. Actors can only learn from those who are better than themselves, which segues nicely into our next area: Directors. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/e0d9d017816c22a3679ec47ccec9fd798b882c5e.png[/img]




[b]Directors [/b]

Unlike Actors, Directors are a more transient portion of the game. They come and go and have limited time frames in which to film a movie. You will always have a low skilled regular director available to make bad movies for you, but the goal will be to build clout and resources to attract the best directors. Your actors cannot learn if they have more talent and gravitas than the director they are working under! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/a57b94c3187fbdd534b8222c92dbf7cb41baf1fb.png[/img]

Directors that focus on a specific genre are better than regular directors, and we have designed it to cycle randomly to help prevent players from being too comfortable. Your studio may have figured out to make great Horror films, but sometimes there isn’t a great Thriller director to make your next slasher flick and you may need to branch out to Romance, Comedy, or Drama. You can mismatch directors with the wrong genre, but your film will suffer. 
 



[b]Staff [/b]

Our final type of employee is your studio staff. Each staff member is hired using clout (and paid using money), and is necessary to unlock certain parts of your technology and assignment trees, as well as other features. They have a solid role in the vanilla version of this game, but we have more plans to expand on staff after launch as we patch in expanded features and consider new mechanics for DLC. As your staff is hired, you will see them start to populate your studio. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36343594/72645ecc15a01b13055e95f2a81c8ce767728d83.png[/img]

notes.title: Developer Diary #1
notes.content:
[i]This developer diary will be mirrored on the [url=http://www.reddit.com/r/MovieMaven]Movie Maven Tycoon subreddit[/url].
[/i]

[b]Movie Maven: A Tycoon Game[/b] has been under active development for close to a year and a half. It is a passion project from a small group of coders and artists who have turned this endeavor into a labor of love. The idea of a detailed management game for a movie studio is not new, and the landscape is littered with failed projects and aborted ideas. We wanted to create a project that was both fun and realistic in scope.

While we have assembled a game that is rich in features, it will take a dedicated base of fans and players to help us balance Movie Maven and make it fun. To participate in the upcoming beta, join our [url=http://www.reddit.com/r/MovieMaven]subreddit[/url] and follow the directions to reach out discord. As we progress through our development diaries (and the beta) we will highlight all the features we have been working on, and the ideas that underpin them. They will include:

[list]
[*]Actors And Directors

[*]Screenplays and Rewrites

[*]Making a Movie

[*]Research and Insights

[*]Building a Distribution Network

[*]Actor Assignments

[*]Events & Staffing

[*]Box Office and Theater Tracking
[/list]

We are extremely excited about this project and we know many of you are as well. We look forward to sharing what we have built and what we plan to add after our launch.

[i]-The Movie Maven Team[/i]
